text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- GOVT TO PROPOSE NEW CORPORATE INCOME TAX TODAY

The government will send Congress a new corporate income tax bill (IRPJ) to be implemented in 1997. The new bill does not alter tax brackets but is designed to increase the tax base. It will also increase the impact of the Financial Operations Tax (IOF) by including factoring companies.
-- IMF CONSIDERS FISCAL SPENDING CUTS INSUFFICIENT

A senior IMF official said the fiscal cuts introduced by the Brazilian government last week, were a step in the right direction but warned the country was still required to move ahead with the constitutional reform program. Teresa Ter-Minassian, of the IMF Fiscal and Monetary Dept said Brazil's operational deficit -- which exceeded $15.7 billion in July -- was still way too high.
-- POLL SHOWS CONDE AHEAD IN RIO MAYORAL RACE

A new Ibope/Rede Globo poll gave Luiz Paulo Conde, the PFL candidate for the second round of the Rio mayoral election, an 18 point lead over PSDB candidate, Sergio Cabral Filho. Forty-seven percent of those polled said they would choose Conde in the Nov 15 election while 29 percent they would vote for Cabral.
-- SOCIAL SECURITY REFORM DELAYED BY MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS

The Senate will only discuss a constitutional amendment to reform Brazil's social security system after the second round of nationwide municipal elections, senators told President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
-- POLICE NEW LIST OF FAKE ACCOUNTS IN NACIONAL

The Federal Police has discovered 1,635 new fake credit accounts in failed Banco Nacional, which closed amidst a $6 billion scandal last year. The new accounts may contain clues to how the bank's management was able to conceal a liquidity crisis for years.
